category_title: Struggling students who rely on step-by-step guided instruction and manipulatives
minimal_context: The student is working one-on-one on math homework involving formulas during an after-school tutoring session.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's get started on your math homework. We have a full hour to work on these formula problems.

STUDENT: I don’t like staying but I know I can get good help—Ms. Haley really does class differently after school.

TUTOR: Go ahead and try the first formula problem on your own.

STUDENT: I really struggle with these. If I have to take this homework home to finish, it usually won't come back the next day.

TUTOR: Just look at the formula on the page and see what you can do.

STUDENT: I can't do it just looking at the formula. I need you to go over the problems step-by-step, or show me the manipulatives so I can see how they relate to my notes.

options.A: Deliver verbal statements or gestures (e.g., high five, thumbs up) indicating approval beyond simple acknowledgment during the after-school tutoring session.
options.B: Break the math formula problems into small chunks for the student to work on during the after-school tutoring session.
options.C: Provide opportunities for the student to respond to the math formula problems at a rate of four to six responses per minute.
options.D: Go over every homework problem with the student, showing him how to use his notes to progress through the work step-by-step.
